title: What a risk is: threats & opportunities
blurb: Define risk, tell threats from opportunities, and describe any risk by its probability and impact.
question: A library refurbishment team notes two things: asbestos might be found behind the old shelving, and a council grant for low-energy lighting might open next spring. Are both of these risks, and how would you describe each one?

teach.body: In APM terms, risk is the potential of an action or event to impact on the achievement of objectives. Put another way: an uncertain event or set of circumstances that, if it occurs, will affect one or more of the project's objectives. In plain English, a risk is something that might happen, has not happened yet, and would make a difference to what the project is trying to achieve if it did.

bands.label: Uncertain: it may or may not happen

teach.caption: Risk sits between the two ends. Something certain not to happen is no risk; something already happening is a fact or an issue, not a risk.

teach.body: Every risk has a PROBABILITY (also called likelihood): how likely it is to occur. And it has an IMPACT: how much it would affect the objectives (time, cost, quality, scope, benefits) if it did occur. Together these two tell you how significant a risk is, which is why risks are later scored and prioritised on both.

teach.caption: APM's definition is neutral: a risk is any uncertainty that would affect objectives, for better or worse.

rows.label: Aim of a response
values: Make it less likely or smaller
Make it more likely or bigger

teach.h: Worked scenario: the Riverside Library refit
teach.body: The team lists two uncertainties. Asbestos might be found behind the old shelving: if it is, work stops for specialist removal, so it is a THREAT with a medium probability and a high impact on time and cost. A council grant for low-energy lighting might open next spring: if it does, the project saves money, so it is an OPPORTUNITY. Both are risks, because neither has happened and both would affect objectives.

rows.label: A key engineer might resign before testing
Exchange rates might move in our favour
The launch date is fixed by law

teach.note: Test: is it uncertain, and would it affect objectives if it happened? Both must be yes.

teach.h: Individual risks and overall project risk
teach.body: An INDIVIDUAL risk is one specific uncertain event, such as 'the crane might be late'. OVERALL project risk is the exposure of the whole project to uncertainty: the combined effect of all the individual risks and other sources of uncertainty. Registers list individual risks; sponsors and boards also care about the overall picture.

teach.text: Two classic distractors: 'a risk is always negative' (wrong: opportunities are risks too) and 'a risk is a problem that has occurred' (wrong: that is an issue). A risk is always UNCERTAIN and always in the FUTURE.

items: Risk: the potential of an action or event to impact on the achievement of objectives.
It is uncertain: it may or may not happen, and it has not happened yet.
A threat would harm objectives; an opportunity would help them.
Every risk is described by its probability (likelihood) and its impact.
Individual risks are single events; overall project risk is the whole project's exposure.

summary: You can now define risk in APM terms, recognise that a risk may be a threat or an opportunity, and describe any risk by its probability and impact. You can also tell a genuine risk apart from something certain or something that has already happened.

A.q: Which of the following best describes a project risk?
options: A problem that is already affecting the work now
A limit on time or cost set by the sponsor
An uncertain event that would affect objectives
A task on the critical path with no float left
A.why: A risk is an uncertain event or set of circumstances that, if it occurs, will affect the project's objectives.

whyNot.0: A problem that is already affecting the work has happened, so it is an issue, not a risk.
whyNot.1: A limit set by the sponsor is a constraint: it is known and certain, not uncertain.
whyNot.3: A critical task with no float is a scheduling fact. It may be a source of risk, but it is not the definition of one.

A.q: A risk that would have a positive effect on the project's objectives if it occurred is known as what?
options: An opportunity
A benefit
A contingency
A threat
A.why: A risk with a positive (beneficial) effect on objectives is an opportunity.

whyNot.1: A benefit is a measurable improvement the project's outputs deliver; it is not an uncertain event.
whyNot.2: A contingency is a reserve of time or money held against risk, not a type of risk.
whyNot.3: A threat is a risk with a negative effect on objectives.

A.q:
Which TWO of the following describe every project risk?
1. A probability of occurring
2. A confirmed cost
3. An impact on objectives if it occurs
4. A named supplier
options: 1 and 2
2 and 4
3 and 4
1 and 3
A.why: Every risk is described by its probability (how likely) and its impact (how much it would affect objectives).

whyNot.0: A confirmed cost would make it certain, which a risk is not.
whyNot.1: Neither a confirmed cost nor a named supplier is a defining feature of a risk.
whyNot.2: Impact is right, but not every risk involves a supplier.

B.q: On a new website project, which of the following is a project risk?
options: The design agency has missed its first deadline
A key developer might leave before the launch
The sponsor has fixed the launch date for May
The budget was overspent in the last period
B.why: The developer leaving is uncertain and in the future, and would affect objectives if it happened, so it is a risk.

whyNot.0: A missed deadline has already happened, so it is an issue rather than a risk.
whyNot.2: A fixed launch date is a constraint: it is certain, not uncertain.
whyNot.3: An overspend that has already occurred is an issue, not a risk.

B.q: In risk management, what does the 'impact' of a risk describe?
options: How likely the risk is to happen at all
When the risk is most likely to occur
Who is responsible for managing the risk
The effect on objectives if it happens
B.why: Impact is the effect the risk would have on objectives (time, cost, quality, scope, benefits) if it occurred.

whyNot.0: How likely a risk is describes its probability (likelihood), not its impact.
whyNot.1: How soon a risk could occur is its proximity, not its impact.
whyNot.2: The person responsible is the risk owner, which is not a measure of the risk itself.

B.q: Which statement about project risk is correct?
options: A risk is always harmful to objectives
A risk is certain to happen at some point
A risk may be a threat or an opportunity
A risk only ever affects the project budget
B.why: APM's definition is neutral: a risk may be a threat (negative) or an opportunity (positive).

whyNot.0: Opportunities are risks with a positive effect, so risks are not always harmful.
whyNot.1: A risk is uncertain: it may or may not happen.
whyNot.3: A risk can affect any objective, including time, quality, scope and benefits.

C.q: A festival team notes that if the weather is fine, on-the-day ticket sales could beat the forecast. How is this best described?
options: An opportunity
An assumption
An issue
A threat
C.why: Higher sales would help objectives and depend on uncertain weather, so this is an opportunity (a positive risk).

whyNot.1: An assumption is something taken to be true for planning; here the team is recording an uncertain upside.
whyNot.2: Nothing has happened yet, so it cannot be an issue.
whyNot.3: A threat would harm objectives; extra sales would help them.

C.q: Which of the following is NOT a feature of a project risk?
options: It has not yet happened to the project
It has a probability of occurring
It is certain to affect the budget
It would affect objectives if it occurs
C.why: A risk is uncertain, so it is never certain to affect anything; and it may affect any objective, not only the budget.

whyNot.0: Being in the future (not yet happened) is a defining feature of a risk.
whyNot.1: Every risk has a probability (likelihood) of occurring.
whyNot.3: A risk, by definition, would affect objectives if it occurred.

C.q: What is the difference between an individual risk and overall project risk?
options: Individual risks are threats; overall risk is upside
Individual risk is one event; overall is total exposure
Individual risks belong to the team; overall to suppliers
Individual risk is scored; overall risk is never assessed
C.why: An individual risk is a single uncertain event; overall project risk is the whole project's exposure to uncertainty, combining all its sources.

whyNot.0: Both individual risks and overall risk can include threats and opportunities.
whyNot.2: Ownership is not what separates the two ideas.
whyNot.3: Overall project risk is assessed too, often by the sponsor and board.

reteach.title: Planning a summer wedding
reteach.question: A couple are planning an outdoor wedding in August. What could go differently from the plan, for better or worse, and which of those things are risks?

blocks.h: What might happen on the day
blocks.body: It might rain on the ceremony: a threat, fairly likely in a British summer, with a big impact on the day. The band might offer a late-booking discount: an opportunity, unlikely but welcome. The venue booking, already confirmed and paid for, is not a risk at all: it is certain. Each risk has a likelihood and an effect; neither has happened yet.

blocks.text: If you can say 'it might', and it would change the outcome, it is a risk. If you can say 'it has' or 'it will definitely', it is not.

explain.body: A risk may or may not happen, and it has not happened yet. Something certain (a confirmed booking, a legal deadline) is not a risk, and something that has already happened is an issue or simply a fact.

test.q: Why is 'the venue is booked and paid for 12 May' not a project risk?
options: It has no owner in the register
It relates to a date, not a cost
It is too small to be worth logging
It is certain, so not uncertain
test.why: A risk must be uncertain. A confirmed, paid booking is certain, so it is a fact, not a risk.

whyNot.0: Having or lacking an owner does not decide whether something is a risk.
whyNot.1: Risks can affect any objective, including time, so a date can still be a risk.
whyNot.2: Size does not decide it: the booking is not a risk because it is certain.

explain.body: A threat would harm objectives if it occurred; an opportunity would help them. Both are risks, because both are uncertain and both would affect objectives. Older or everyday usage treats 'risk' as only bad news; APM does not.

test.q: A cheaper material might become available mid-project, cutting costs. How is this best described?
options: A threat with a low impact
A constraint on the design
An opportunity for the project
An issue for the sponsor to resolve
test.why: It is uncertain and would help the cost objective, so it is an opportunity.

whyNot.0: A threat would harm objectives; lower costs help them.
whyNot.1: A constraint is a fixed limit, not an uncertain event.
whyNot.3: Nothing has happened yet, so it is not an issue.

explain.body: Probability (likelihood) asks how likely the risk is to happen. Impact asks how much it would affect objectives if it did. A risk that is very likely but trivial, and one that is rare but disastrous, need different attention.

test.q: Which TWO measures are used to describe how significant a risk is?
options: Cost and duration of work
Probability and impact
Owner and status
Cause and category
test.why: A risk's significance comes from its probability (likelihood) combined with its impact on objectives.

whyNot.0: Cost and duration are objectives a risk might affect, not measures of the risk.
whyNot.2: Owner and status are register fields used to manage a risk, not to size it.
whyNot.3: Cause and category help describe and group risks, but do not measure their significance.

explain.body: Risk only matters because of what it would do to the project's objectives. An uncertain event that would make no difference to time, cost, quality, scope or benefits is not a project risk. That is why risk is always defined in terms of its effect on objectives.

test.q: Complete the statement: risk is defined by its potential effect on the project's ______.
options: objectives
suppliers
stakeholders
team morale
test.why: Risk is the potential of an action or event to impact on the achievement of objectives.

whyNot.1: Suppliers can be a source of risk, but the definition is about the effect on objectives.
whyNot.2: Stakeholders may be affected, but the definition is framed around objectives.
whyNot.3: Morale might be a cause of risk; the definition centres on objectives.
